land.text: 'a confederation of eight Xiongnu tribes in Bi's power base in the south ... seceded from Punu's kingdom'

predecessors.note: The xiongnu dossier (ia-01-a) carries the matching split event of 48; the Northern Xiongnu continue under Punu.

land.text: the Southern Xiongnu's frontier land in Shanxi, Shaanxi and Inner Mongolia, reorganized in 216 'into the Five Divisions'

successors.note: Cao Cao, then King of Wei (Cliopatria 'Cao Cao' 197-223, dossier cao-cao). The Five Divisions plotted to break away and acclaimed Liu Yuan in 304, whose Han (later Zhao) is Cliopatria's Former Zhao (306-336); that is a new state, not this one.

capitals.name: Meiji, Xihe Commandery (Ordos, Inner Mongolia)
capitals.note: The page says the chanyu 'was ordered to court at Meiji County, Xihe Commandery' (undated; the year 50 is that of the submission to Han). Coordinates approximate (Zhungeer, Ordos); the page names no coordinates.

correction.text: Bi's power base in the south and the eight frontier commanderies, as Cliopatria draws it from 51

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 48-50: the Southern Xiongnu begin in 48 ('a confederation of eight Xiongnu tribes in Bi's power base in the south' acclaimed Bi as chanyu), three years before Cliopatria's first shape; the 51 shape is carried back unchanged. The page gives no boundary.

187,257 km2, 51-59 (103.4-115.0 E, 38.6-42.6 N, the Ordos, Hetao and Yinshan side of Inner Mongolia). The page: 40,000 to 50,000 men and 'his followers were resettled in eight frontier commanderies' (undated); no area figure for the Southern Xiongnu (the infobox is for the whole confederation), so the shape is unverified in extent.

186,875 km2, 60-90. Same land; in June 89 'the main army of the Southern Xiongnu' marched with the Han against the Northern Xiongnu and in early 90 chanyu Tuntuhe attacked them again (Ikh Bayan page); no border change.

186,818 km2, 91-105. Same land. Cliopatria's row ends in 105, but the page has the Southern Xiongnu in the record in 188 ('against the Wuhuan in Hebei'), 195 (Huchuquan succeeds his brother) and 216; see southern-xiongnu_106.

correction.text: the 91 shape carried forward: the Southern Xiongnu's frontier commanderies until 216

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 106-215, no Cliopatria shape: the 91 shape is carried forward. The Xiongnu page has the Southern Xiongnu 'against the Wuhuan in Hebei in 188', Huchuquan succeeding his brother 'in 195' and Cao Cao reorganizing 'the last vestiges of the Southern Xiongnu into the Five Divisions' in 216; it names no land beyond Meiji County in Xihe Commandery and 'eight frontier commanderies', so the extent is unverified. Overlap: Cliopatria's Xianbei shapes of 106-196 and the xianbei dossier's keyframes from 91 cover about 203-213 k of this shape's 216 k km2; the two dossiers must agree on who holds the Ordos-Hetao frontier in 91-216. (reviewer ia-01-b, 2026-10-18)

region.text: Bi's power base in the south and the eight frontier commanderies, as Cliopatria draws it from 51

ledger.note: 48: eight Xiongnu tribes in the south acclaim Bi as chanyu. 'In 48 AD, a confederation of eight Xiongnu tribes in Bi's power base in the south' seceded from Punu's kingdom, 40,000 to 50,000 men; in 50 AD 'the Southern Xiongnu submitted to tributary relations with Han China' and his followers were 'resettled in eight frontier commanderies'. The page names the base, not a boundary. Confidence 2: the page names Bi's base and the eight frontier commanderies, not a boundary. (reviewer ia-01-b, 2026-10-18)

region.text: the Southern Xiongnu's frontier land in 216

ledger.note: 216: Cao Cao breaks the Southern Xiongnu into the Five Divisions. 'reorganized the last vestiges of the Southern Xiongnu into the Five Divisions' in 216; the Five Divisions acclaimed Liu Yuan in 304. The shape is the researcher's reading of the frontier commanderies. Confidence 2: the page names the Five Divisions, not their land; the shape is the researcher's reading. (reviewer ia-01-b, 2026-10-18)

wars.name: Southern Xiongnu against the Northern Xiongnu
wars.outcome: The Northern Xiongnu 'was dealt a heavy defeat' by the Southern in 49; the Southern Xiongnu allied with the Xianbei in 85 and marched with the Han in June 89 (Altai) and again in early 90 under chanyu Tuntuhe, who 'captured his rival's seal, treasure, wives and daughters'; Han and Xianbei finished the Northern state in 91.
wars.note: The Xiongnu page gives 49 and says the Southern Xiongnu 'played a role in defeating the Northern Xiongnu'; the Xianbei alliance of 85 is on the Xianbei page. The land won belongs to the Han and Xianbei in the xiongnu and xianbei dossiers, not to the Southern Xiongnu.

certainty.note: A tributary people settled in Han frontier commanderies: the commandery lines are not on the pages opened, and the shape is Cliopatria's approximation.

sources.title: Xiongnu
sources.note: The split of 48, submission to Han in 50, Meiji, 40,000-50,000 men, 188, 195, 216, 304-328; the Southern and Northern Xiongnu redirect here.

sources.title: Battle of Ikh Bayan
sources.note: The Southern Xiongnu army in the 89 expedition and Tuntuhe's attack of early 90; the Northern remnants left in Dzungaria.

notes: Different state from the xiongnu dossier (Q188836 is shared): the Southern Xiongnu seceded in 48, became a Han tributary in 50 and were settled in eight frontier commanderies; the Northern Xiongnu continue under Punu (xiongnu dossier, which lists this one as the 48 split and expects the 50 CE Han vassal_start). Cliopatria's row (51-105) is extended to 48 at the start and to 216 at the end because the page has the Southern Xiongnu until Cao Cao's reorganization of 216; both extensions carry the 51 and 91 shapes unchanged and are unverified in extent. The (Alliance between Han Dynasty and Xiongnu) relation row, 30..105 in Cliopatria, belongs here, not to the Northern Xiongnu. For other dossiers: the han-dynasty dossier (ea-02) should carry a vassal_start in 50 (counterpart southern-xiongnu, page 'submitted to tributary relations with Han China') and the end of it in 216; the cao-cao dossier (ea-03) should carry the 216 Five Divisions. Not on the page: Wuyuan, Dingxiang, Shang and Beidi commanderies, the Southern Xiongnu revolts of 94 and 140 (the 94 revolt on the page is the Northern Xiongnu's), and anything on the 188 death of the chanyu beyond 'against the Wuhuan in Hebei in 188'. The Xiongnu page has no Southern Xiongnu population or area figure; the Cliopatria 187 k km2 is not checked against an infobox. Page budget: two pages (Xiongnu, Battle of Ikh Bayan). No unknown gazetteer names.
